sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Treasury withdrawal for the design, implementation, security audit, and ecosystem adoption of an open-source OpenZeppelin development stack for Cardano.
Recipient: OpenZeppelin for delivery, administered by Intersect

Deliverables: Three Reference Implementations: Cardano Liquid Staking Protocol, Self-Repaying Loans Protocol, and Tokenized Money Market Fund, OpenZeppelin Contracts Library for Cardano, Contracts Wizard, UI Builder, AI-enhanced development tools, and Cardano documentation, Security retainer covering audits, reviews, penetration testing, and published findings, Developer enablement and co-marketing program
Deadline/expiry: Twelve months across four quarterly milestones from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027, commencing after the legal contract is signed

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal requests a total treasury withdrawal of 11,787,063 ada, consisting of 11,443,750 ada for delivery and a 343,313 ada Intersect administration fee.
Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The delivery budget is stated as USD $1,831,000 over 12 months, calculated at a reference rate of USD 0.16 per ada.

Claim (governance, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal includes milestone-based disbursement, with a 20% kick-off payment after legal sign-off and four equal 20% milestone payments after evidence submission and Intersect Delivery Assurance approval.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): OpenZeppelin proposes to deliver three end-to-end Cardano Reference Implementations covering liquid staking, self-repaying loans, and a tokenized money market fund.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): OpenZeppelin proposes a secure, audited, documented Cardano contracts library with components including access control, cryptographic utilities, DeFi primitives, governance, credentials, multi-sig, vesting, messaging, and a Cardano Contract ABI.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): OpenZeppelin will dedicate 22 researcher-weeks of security capacity over 12 months and publish security findings and reports alongside audited releases.
missing: Independent evidence for: The proposer claims OpenZeppelin Contracts have enabled over $36 trillion in value transferred, $110B+ TVL importing the contracts, about 85% market share in top 50 DeFi protocols, and 5.9B+ transactions since 2018.
Independent evidence for: OpenZeppelin discloses that it has not received Cardano Treasury ada within the prior 24 months and has not received Project Catalyst funding.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "The proposal requests a total treasury withdrawal of 11,787,063 ada, consisting of 11,443,750 ada for delivery and a 343,313 ada Intersect administration fee." though 1 review blocker(s) remain open.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "The proposer claims OpenZeppelin Contracts have enabled over $36 trillion in value transferred, $110B+ TVL importing the contracts, about 85% market share in top 50 DeFi protocols, and 5.9B+ transactions since 2018." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: evidence is too thin for a directional vote while 1 blocker(s) remain open.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
